title: Gone fishing, for bicycles: the strange catch of Amsterdam's canals

words.zh: 捕获物、渔获；隐藏的问题
words.note: a good catch（收获颇丰）。口语 What's the catch?（有什么猫腻？）之前学过 there is a catch（其中有诈）。
words.ctx: Gone fishing, for bicycles: the strange catch of Amsterdam's canals

ex.en: The fishermen brought home a big [[catch]].
ex.zh: 渔民们满载而归。

ex.en: Today's [[catch]] includes two old bikes and a chair.
ex.zh: 今天的“渔获”有两辆旧自行车和一把椅子。

cloze.before: Gone fishing, for bicycles: the strange
cloze.after: of Amsterdam's canals
cloze.szh: 去钓鱼，钓自行车：阿姆斯特丹运河里的奇特“渔获”

words.note: haul sth out of / up：把重物拖出来、拉上来。名词 haul 也指“一大批（收获）”：a big haul of shopping。
words.ctx: Every year a small crane boat hauls thousands of bikes out of the city's waterways.

ex.en: They [[hauled]] the boat onto the beach.
ex.zh: 他们把船拖上了沙滩。

ex.en: Firefighters [[hauled]] the car out of the river.
ex.zh: 消防员把车从河里拖了出来。

cloze.before: Every year a small crane boat

cloze.szh: 每年，一艘带起重机的小船都会从城里的水道中捞出成千上万辆自行车。

words.note: 运河、河流等可以行船的水路。inland waterways（内陆水道）。
words.ctx: Every year a small crane boat hauls thousands of bikes out of the city's waterways.

ex.en: The city is crossed by narrow [[waterways]].
ex.zh: 城市里纵横交错着狭窄的水道。

ex.en: Boats are the best way to see the [[waterways]].
ex.zh: 坐船是游览水道的最好方式。

words.note: A outnumber B：A 比 B 多。Women outnumber men in this class.（这个班女生比男生多。）
words.ctx: The catch says a lot about a country where bicycles outnumber people.

ex.en: Tourists [[outnumber]] locals in summer.
ex.zh: 夏天游客比本地人还多。

ex.en: We were [[outnumbered]] three to one.
ex.zh: 对方人数是我们的三倍。

cloze.before: The catch says a lot about a country where bicycles
cloze.after: people.
cloze.szh: 这些“渔获”很能说明一个自行车比人还多的国家是什么样子。

words.note: 平稳、安静地移动：a swan glides across the lake（天鹅滑过湖面）。
words.ctx: On a grey weekday morning, a flat boat glides along a canal in central Amsterdam, its crane arm dipping into the murky water.

ex.en: The skater [[glided]] across the ice.
ex.zh: 滑冰的人在冰上滑过。

ex.en: A plane [[glides]] down to the runway.
ex.zh: 飞机滑翔着降向跑道。

ex.en: She [[dipped]] her toes in the water.
ex.zh: 她把脚趾探进水里。

ex.en: [[Dip]] the bread in the soup.
ex.zh: 把面包蘸到汤里。

ex.en: The river was too [[murky]] to see the bottom.

ex.en: The details of the deal remain [[murky]].
ex.zh: 这笔交易的细节仍然不清不楚。

words.note: a tangle of wires / hair（一团乱线 / 乱发）。形容词 tangled（缠在一起的）。
words.ctx: Moments later it surfaces with a dripping tangle of metal: handlebars, wheels and a bike lock still firmly fastened.

ex.en: There was a [[tangle]] of cables behind the TV.
ex.zh: 电视后面是一团乱糟糟的电线。

ex.en: My headphones are always [[tangled]].
ex.zh: 我的耳机线总是缠在一起。

ex.en: Please [[fasten]] your seat belt.
ex.zh: 请系好安全带。

ex.en: The gate was [[fastened]] with a chain.
ex.zh: 大门用铁链锁着。

words.note: 不可数。车祸、空难、船难之后的残骸。wreck（残骸、破旧的东西）是可数名词。
words.ctx: The crew pile the wreckage onto the deck and move on to the next spot.

ex.en: Rescuers searched the [[wreckage]].
ex.zh: 救援人员在残骸中搜寻。

ex.en: [[Wreckage]] from the boat washed up on the beach.
ex.zh: 船的残骸被冲上了海滩。

words.note: pile up（堆积）。名词 a pile of books（一堆书）。
words.ctx: The crew pile the wreckage onto the deck and move on to the next spot.

ex.en: Dirty dishes [[piled]] up in the sink.
ex.zh: 脏碗碟堆满了水槽。

ex.en: She [[piled]] the books on the table.
ex.zh: 她把书堆在桌上。

words.note: move on to the next question（进入下一个问题）。也可以比喻“放下过去”：It's time to move on.
words.ctx: The crew pile the wreckage onto the deck and move on to the next spot.

ex.en: Let's [[move on]] to the next topic.
ex.zh: 我们进入下一个话题吧。

ex.en: After the break-up, she found it hard to [[move on]].
ex.zh: 分手后，她很难走出来。

words.zh: 最终（到某处、处于某种状态）
words.note: end up + 地点 / doing / 形容词：We ended up eating at home.（我们最后在家吃了。）
words.ctx: How so many bikes end up in the water is a matter of some debate.

ex.en: We got lost and [[ended up]] in the wrong town.
ex.zh: 我们迷了路，最后到了另一个镇。

ex.en: If you don't save, you'll [[end up]] broke.
ex.zh: 你不存钱，最后会身无分文。

cloze.before: How so many bikes
cloze.after: up in the water is a matter of some debate.

words.note: a matter of + 名词：……的问题。a matter of taste（口味问题）、a matter of time（时间问题）。
words.ctx: How so many bikes end up in the water is a matter of some debate.

ex.en: Who invented it first is [[a matter of debate]].
ex.zh: 谁先发明的还有争议。

ex.en: Its real age is [[a matter of some debate]].
ex.zh: 它真正的年代还有一些争议。

cloze.hint: 有争议的问题（a matter of some ___）

words.zh: 倾倒、随意丢弃；甩掉（恋人）
words.note: dump rubbish（乱倒垃圾）。口语 dump sb（甩了某人）。名词 a dump（垃圾场；脏乱的地方）。
words.ctx: Some are stolen, ridden around and then dumped; others are pushed in by pranksters after a night out.

ex.en: Someone [[dumped]] an old sofa by the road.
ex.zh: 有人把一张旧沙发扔在路边。

ex.en: He was [[dumped]] by text message.
ex.zh: 他是被短信分手的。

words.ctx: Some are stolen, ridden around and then dumped; others are pushed in by pranksters after a night out.

ex.en: A [[prankster]] put a traffic cone on the statue.
ex.zh: 一个恶作剧的人把路锥扣在了雕像头上。

ex.en: The kids played a [[prank]] on their teacher.
ex.zh: 孩子们捉弄了他们的老师。

words.note: have a night out with friends（和朋友出去玩一晚）。反义 a night in（在家过夜）。
words.ctx: Some are stolen, ridden around and then dumped; others are pushed in by pranksters after a night out.

ex.en: We had [[a night out]] for her birthday.
ex.zh: 我们为她过生日出去玩了一晚。

ex.en: After [[a night out]], he slept until noon.
ex.zh: 晚上出去玩了以后，他一觉睡到中午。

words.zh: 残骸；破旧不堪的东西（或人）
words.note: 可数：an old wreck（一辆破车）。口语形容人：I'm a wreck today.（我今天累垮了。）动词 wreck：毁坏。
words.ctx: A few slip in by accident when they are parked too close to the edge, and some owners, tired of an old wreck, simply leave theirs to the water.

ex.en: His first car was an old [[wreck]].
ex.zh: 他的第一辆车是辆破车。

ex.en: The storm [[wrecked]] the garden.
ex.zh: 暴风雨毁了花园。

cloze.after: , simply leave theirs to the water.
cloze.szh: 有少数是停得离岸边太近，不小心滑下去的；还有些车主嫌旧车破，干脆把它交给了河水。

words.note: a layer of dust（一层灰），wear layers（穿多层衣服）。
words.ctx: Locals joke that there are three layers at the bottom of each canal: mud, bikes and then more mud.

ex.en: The table was covered in a thick [[layer]] of dust.
ex.zh: 桌子上落了厚厚一层灰。

ex.en: Wear [[layers]] when you go hiking.
ex.zh: 去徒步要穿得一层一层的。

cloze.szh: 当地人开玩笑说，每条运河底部都有三层：泥、自行车，然后还是泥。

words.note: on a large scale（大规模地），the scale of the problem（问题的严重程度）。地图上的比例尺也叫 scale。
words.ctx: The scale of cycling in the Netherlands helps explain the problem.

ex.en: Nobody expected the [[scale]] of the damage.
ex.zh: 没人料到破坏的程度这么大。

ex.en: The festival is held on a huge [[scale]].
ex.zh: 这个节日规模盛大。

cloze.before: The
cloze.after: of cycling in the Netherlands helps explain the problem.
cloze.szh: 荷兰骑车人数的规模，有助于解释这个问题。

words.note: batter（连续猛击）的过去分词作形容词：a battered old suitcase（一个破旧的老箱子）。
words.ctx: The country has an estimated 23 million bicycles for 18 million people, and in cities many residents own two: a good one for long rides and a battered one for leaving at the station.

ex.en: He still drives a [[battered]] old van.
ex.zh: 他还开着一辆破旧的面包车。

ex.en: She carries a [[battered]] notebook everywhere.
ex.zh: 她走到哪儿都带着一本破旧的笔记本。

cloze.szh: 这个国家估计有 2300 万辆自行车，而人口只有 1800 万；在城市里，很多居民有两辆：一辆好车骑远路，一辆破车停在车站。

words.note: That's precisely the point.（这正是问题所在。）也表示“准确地”：at precisely 9 o'clock（九点整）。
words.ctx: The second kind is rarely locked with much care, which is precisely what makes it a target.

ex.zh: 这正是我给你打电话的原因。

ex.en: The train left at [[precisely]] six.
ex.zh: 火车六点整准时开出。

words.note: an easy target（容易得手的目标），hit a target（达到目标）。动词：target young people（针对年轻人）。
words.ctx: The second kind is rarely locked with much care, which is precisely what makes it a target.

ex.en: Tourists are an easy [[target]] for pickpockets.
ex.zh: 游客很容易成为小偷的目标。

ex.en: We hit our sales [[target]] this month.
ex.zh: 这个月我们达到了销售目标。

words.note: 本义“头疼”：I have a headache. 比喻：Traffic is a real headache.（交通真让人头疼。）
words.ctx: Parking is a constant headache.

ex.en: Finding a babysitter is always a [[headache]].
ex.zh: 找保姆总是件头疼的事。

ex.en: I woke up with a terrible [[headache]].
ex.zh: 我醒来时头疼得厉害。

cloze.before: Parking is a constant
cloze.szh: 停车一直是个让人头疼的问题。

words.note: 英式拼法，storey = 楼层。a multi-storey car park（多层停车场）。美式写 multi-story。
words.ctx: Utrecht's main station now has a multi-storey garage with room for 12,500 bikes, reputedly the largest in the world, and it still fills up on busy days.

ex.en: We parked in a [[multi-storey]] car park.
ex.zh: 我们把车停在了一个多层停车场。

ex.en: The old [[multi-storey]] building was pulled down.
ex.zh: 那栋老旧的多层楼被拆了。

cloze.before: Utrecht's main station now has a
cloze.after: garage with room for 12,500 bikes, reputedly the largest in the world, and it still fills up on busy days.
cloze.szh: 乌得勒支中央车站如今有一座多层自行车库，可停放 12,500 辆车，据说是世界最大的，可在忙碌的日子里还是会停满。

words.note: reputation（名声）相关。The house is reputedly haunted.（据说这房子闹鬼。）比学过的 reportedly（据报道）更偏“传闻、名声”。
words.ctx: Utrecht's main station now has a multi-storey garage with room for 12,500 bikes, reputedly the largest in the world, and it still fills up on busy days.

ex.en: The restaurant [[reputedly]] serves the best pasta in town.
ex.zh: 据说这家餐厅的意面是全城最好吃的。

ex.en: He is [[reputedly]] the richest man in the village.
ex.zh: 据说他是村里最有钱的人。

cloze.after: the largest in the world, and it still fills up on busy days.
cloze.szh: 乌得勒支中央车站如今有一座多层自行车库，可停放 12,500 辆车，据说是世界最大的，可在忙碌的日子里还是会停满。

words.note: bus depot（公交总站）。注意发音：英式 /ˈdepəʊ/，t 不发音。
words.ctx: The bikes are taken to a depot, where the few that are registered can be traced back to their owners.

ex.en: The buses return to the [[depot]] at night.
ex.zh: 公交车晚上开回总站。

ex.en: Lost bikes are kept at a [[depot]] near the port.
ex.zh: 丢失的自行车存放在港口附近的一个仓库里。

cloze.before: The bikes are taken to a
cloze.after: , where the few that are registered can be traced back to their owners.
cloze.szh: 自行车被运到一个仓库，其中少数登记过的可以追查到车主。

words.note: trace sth back to sb / sth：追查到……。The problem was traced back to a faulty cable.（问题追查到一根坏电线。）
words.ctx: The bikes are taken to a depot, where the few that are registered can be traced back to their owners.

ex.en: The fire was [[traced back to]] a candle.
ex.zh: 火灾追查到是一支蜡烛引起的。

ex.en: Her family can be [[traced back to]] the 1600s.

words.note: scrap an old car（报废旧车）。也指取消计划：The plan was scrapped.（计划取消了。）名词 scrap metal（废金属）。
words.ctx: The rest are scrapped and the metal is recycled, sometimes ending up in new bicycles.

ex.en: The old trains will be [[scrapped]].
ex.zh: 旧火车将被报废。

ex.en: They [[scrapped]] the idea after one meeting.
ex.zh: 开了一次会，他们就放弃了这个主意。

cloze.before: The rest are
cloze.after: and the metal is recycled, sometimes ending up in new bicycles.
cloze.szh: 其余的被当作废品处理，金属回收再利用，有时最后又变成了新的自行车。

words.note: recycle paper / plastic / glass。名词 recycling（回收）。
words.ctx: The rest are scrapped and the metal is recycled, sometimes ending up in new bicycles.

ex.en: We [[recycle]] all our bottles.
ex.zh: 我们的瓶子全部回收利用。

ex.en: This bag is made of [[recycled]] plastic.
ex.zh: 这个袋子是用回收塑料做的。

cloze.before: The rest are scrapped and the metal is
cloze.after: , sometimes ending up in new bicycles.
cloze.szh: 其余的被当作废品处理，金属回收再利用，有时最后又变成了新的自行车。

words.expr: not so much A as B
words.zh: 与其说是 A，不如说是 B
words.note: 否定 A 的说法，强调 B 才更准确：He is not so much shy as quiet.（与其说他害羞，不如说他安静。）A 和 B 词性要对等。
words.ctx: Seen this way, the canal fishermen are not so much cleaning up a mess as closing a loop.

ex.en: It's [[not so much]] a job as a hobby.
ex.zh: 与其说这是工作，不如说是爱好。

ex.en: She was [[not so much]] angry as disappointed.
ex.zh: 与其说她生气，不如说她失望。

words.conn: not so much + A + as + B（A、B 结构相同）

pick.q: The problem is not so much the money ___ the time.
pick.why: 固定搭配 not so much A as B，后面用 as，不用 than。

pick.q: He didn't so much walk ___ run out of the room.
pick.why: not so much ... as ... 也可以把 not 放在助动词上：didn't so much walk as run（与其说是走，不如说是跑）。

cloze.before: Seen this way, the canal fishermen are not so
cloze.after: cleaning up a mess as closing a loop.
cloze.szh: 这样看来，这些运河“渔夫”与其说是在收拾烂摊子，不如说是在让资源循环起来。

words.note: 比 happy 程度深：I'm delighted to meet you. be delighted by / with / at：因……而高兴。
words.ctx: Visitors often stop to film the crane at work, delighted by such an odd spectacle.

ex.en: I'd be [[delighted]] to help.
ex.zh: 我非常乐意帮忙。

ex.en: The children were [[delighted]] with the puppy.
ex.zh: 孩子们看到小狗高兴坏了。

cloze.before: Visitors often stop to film the crane at work,
cloze.after: by such an odd spectacle.
cloze.szh: 游客常常停下来拍吊臂干活，被这种奇特的景象逗乐了。

words.zh: 景象、奇观；（引人注目的）场面
words.note: 注意和学过的形容词 spectacular（壮观的）区分。make a spectacle of oneself：当众出丑。
words.ctx: Visitors often stop to film the crane at work, delighted by such an odd spectacle.

ex.en: The fireworks were a wonderful [[spectacle]].
ex.zh: 烟花真是壮观的景象。

ex.en: The fight in the street became a public [[spectacle]].
ex.zh: 街头斗殴成了众人围观的场面。

cloze.before: Visitors often stop to film the crane at work, delighted by such an odd
cloze.szh: 游客常常停下来拍吊臂干活，被这种奇特的景象逗乐了。

words.note: 名词：my morning routine（我每天早上的固定流程）。形容词：a routine check（例行检查）。
words.ctx: For residents it is merely routine, as unremarkable as rubbish collection.

ex.en: Exercise is part of my daily [[routine]].
ex.zh: 锻炼是我每天的固定安排。

ex.en: It was just a [[routine]] check.
ex.zh: 那只是一次例行检查。

cloze.before: For residents it is merely
cloze.after: , as unremarkable as rubbish collection.
cloze.szh: 对居民来说，这只是例行公事，就像收垃圾一样稀松平常。

words.note: un-（不）+ remarkable（值得注意的、了不起的）。
words.ctx: For residents it is merely routine, as unremarkable as rubbish collection.

ex.en: The town itself is fairly [[unremarkable]].
ex.zh: 这个小镇本身相当平淡无奇。

ex.en: He had an [[unremarkable]] childhood.
ex.zh: 他的童年平平无奇。

cloze.before: For residents it is merely routine, as
cloze.after: as rubbish collection.
cloze.szh: 对居民来说，这只是例行公事，就像收垃圾一样稀松平常。

words.note: sentimental（多愁善感的、感情用事的）的反义。an unsentimental view of life（对人生务实的看法）。
words.ctx: Yet the sight of a bicycle rising from a canal says something about the Dutch: practical, unsentimental and quietly amused by their own habits.

ex.en: She is [[unsentimental]] about throwing old things away.
ex.zh: 扔旧东西的时候她一点也不感情用事。

ex.en: The film gives an [[unsentimental]] picture of war.
ex.zh: 这部电影冷静地展现了战争。

cloze.before: Yet the sight of a bicycle rising from a canal says something about the Dutch: practical,
cloze.after: and quietly amused by their own habits.
cloze.szh: 可一辆自行车从运河里升起来的画面，也透露出荷兰人的一些特点：务实、不感情用事，对自己的习惯还暗暗觉得好笑。

words.note: It's only a matter of time before ...：……只是迟早的事。
words.ctx: In a city built on water and wheels, it was only a matter of time before the two met.

ex.en: It's only [[a matter of time]] before he finds out.
ex.zh: 他发现只是迟早的事。

ex.en: Success is [[a matter of time]].
ex.zh: 成功只是时间问题。

cloze.before: In a city built on water and wheels, it was only a matter of
cloze.after: before the two met.
cloze.szh: 在一座建在水与车轮之上的城市里，两者相遇只是时间问题。
